drawStars.name: Draw a pyramid of stars
drawStars.description: Write a layoutStars function that takes a number of rows and builds an array of strings where each string has one fewer star than the last, then draws it with drawStars. For example, layoutStars(3) draws the pyramid for ["***", "**", "*"].

count1.name: Count is 1
count1.description: A count of one draws a single star.

count3.name: Count is 3
count3.description: A count of three draws a three-row pyramid.

count5.name: Count is 5
count5.description: A count of five draws a five-row pyramid.

count10.name: Count is 10
count10.description: A count of ten draws a ten-row pyramid.

shapeOfAnswer.question: What am I building?
shapeOfAnswer.answer: An array of strings, longest first, each one a star shorter than the one before, down to a single star. When it's drawn, the longest row sits at the bottom of the pyramid. Build the whole array first, then draw it with `drawStars`.

countingDown.question: How do I make each row shorter than the last?
countingDown.answer: The lengths need to go down: the first string is the longest and the last is a single star. A loop that counts down from the total to 1 hands you each length in turn.

buildingEachRow.question: How do I build a string with a certain number of stars?
buildingEachRow.answer: Start with an empty string and add one `*` at a time until it's the right length. Then `push` that string onto your array before moving to the next row.
